video.title: The Magic of Single-Foot Forehand Training

classification.reason: The coach and a demonstrator use a single-foot probing exercise to teach foot loading, spatial probing, and contact zone adjustments on the forehand.

problem.title_as_question: How can single-foot training improve forehand probing and weight transfer?
problem.definition: Players often fail to run deep enough and load behind the ball with their outside foot, leading to arm-reaching swings without body drive, and struggle to visually adjust when caught out of position.
prerequisites: basic open or semi-open forehand stance mechanics
ability to balance and hop on one foot

symptoms.description: Reaching with the arm and curling the ball around instead of driving through the court.
Absence of weight transfer through the court as the body cannot press out of the corner.
Excessive leaning and upper body compensations to make contact on poorly probed balls.
Contact point ends up too close to the body or overly stretched away from the ideal slot.

causes.statement: The outside loading foot fails to get deep enough into the corner and behind the ball.
The loading foot cannot push through the court, preventing any forward weight transfer.
Imperfect visual tracking and probing ability fail to position the body in its optimal contact orientation.

angles.summary: The loading foot must position behind the ball so it can press through the court and unload body weight into the shot.
Comparing a rep with insufficient corner depth against a rep loaded cleanly behind the ball, showing natural body unloading.
Hitting from a balanced loading position feels like explosive weight transfer, whereas improper positioning feels like weak arm curling.
Contrasting an advanced player's identical, well-probed swings with the coach's varied, body-compensating swings due to imperfect tracking.
Tracking the ball continuously with the eyes allows the player to recognize its actual location and deliver the racket through it.
Debunking the idea that you should take the exact same mechanical swing regardless of position rather than actively adjusting to the ball.

solutions.summary: Probe and hit forehands while balancing and moving on one foot instead of two to train foot placement and tracking.
solutions.external_goal: Probe the fed ball and hit while balancing on a single foot.

solutions.summary: Get behind the ball and deep enough into the corner so you can press your body weight back out through the court.
solutions.external_goal: Press out of the corner towards the crosscourt target.

solutions.summary: Look at the ball and swing through the ball that you see rather than blindly taking an identical swing when poorly probed.
solutions.external_goal: Look at the incoming ball and swing through its seen position.

solutions.summary: Adjust your body posture to preserve roughly the same swing through the contact hitting zone even when spacing is off.
solutions.external_goal: Maintain the same swing trajectory through the contact hitting zone.
